task_title: Ship aider and goose adapters so every harness the spec names has one
task_criteria: scripts/harness/install-aider.sh and install-goose.sh exist and are executable; each --check prints named PASS/FAIL/WARN rows plus exactly ONE verdict line (AIDER:/GOOSE:) whose label and exit code are derived from its own row counts, matching install-deepseek.sh (FAIL (1) exit 1 when no binary is installed), and places nothing on disk FAILIF: either --check prints zero verdict lines, a verdict line that contradicts its own FAIL/WARN counts, exit 0/PASS while its binary row reads FAIL, or creates a file in a scratch HOME PROOF: bash scripts/harness/install-aider.sh --check; bash scripts/harness/install-goose.sh --check with output and exit codes pasted

each --apply exits 1 with a named 'FAIL apply — refused' row stating the ladder is unmeasured, and places no executable in a scratch HOME FAILIF: --apply exits 0, installs anything, or refuses without naming the unmeasured ladder PROOF: env -i PATH=$PATH HOME=$(mktemp -d) bash scripts/harness/install-aider.sh --apply; same for goose; find of the scratch HOME shows 0 executables

tests/harness-conformance.sh HARNESSES lists aider and goose so the battery emits a row per harness, and the battery's fail count grows only by those two binary-absent rows (baseline at 6d1d717: 15 pass, 3 fail, 11 skip) FAILIF: the battery emits no aider/goose row or any third harness regresses from pass to fail PROOF: bash tests/harness-conformance.sh at the base ref and at the fix head, both summaries pasted

specs/HARNESS.md (adapter table, closing paragraph, --check table), README.md and docs/handbook/chapters/M5-harness.md state the new truth: both ship a real --check/--contract, --apply refuses by name, still unmeasured FAILIF: any of the three still says aider and goose ship no adapter file PROOF: grep -n 'no adapter file' specs/HARNESS.md README.md docs/handbook/chapters/M5-harness.md returns nothing for aider/goose

tests/selftest.sh carries a numbered cell that asserts the verdict LETTERS and exit codes for both arms and both harnesses, and bash tests/selftest.sh ends SELFTEST: PASS FAILIF: selftest ends FAIL (n), or the new cell passes with an adapter whose verdict contradicts its rows PROOF: bash tests/selftest.sh output tail showing the cell's PASS rows and SELFTEST: PASS

both new adapters carry a ch:trace CF-006 marker in their header FAILIF: grep -L 'ch:trace' on either file returns the file PROOF: grep -c 'ch:trace' scripts/harness/install-aider.sh scripts/harness/install-goose.sh

items.criterion: scripts/harness/install-aider.sh and install-goose.sh exist and are executable; each --check prints named PASS/FAIL/WARN rows plus exactly ONE verdict line (AIDER:/GOOSE:) whose label and exit code are derived from its own row counts, matching install-deepseek.sh (FAIL (1) exit 1 when no binary is installed), and places nothing on disk
items.detail: `ls -l` shows both files mode -rwxrwxr-x. `bash scripts/harness/install-aider.sh --check` prints `  FAIL  binary — absent — no aider in this node …` then exactly one verdict line `AIDER: FAIL (1)` with EXIT=1; goose prints `GOOSE: FAIL (1)` EXIT=1. The verdict comes from the shared scripts/lib.sh verdict() (FAILED>0 -> "LABEL: FAIL (n)", return 1), the same function install-deepseek.sh uses, and each adapter ends `verdict AIDER; exit $?` (install-aider.sh:110, install-goose.sh:111). Scratch HOME after both --check runs: `find $H -mindepth 1 | wc -l` = 0.

items.criterion: each --apply exits 1 with a named 'FAIL apply — refused' row stating the ladder is unmeasured, and places no executable in a scratch HOME
items.detail: `env -i PATH=$PATH HOME=$(mktemp -d) bash scripts/harness/install-aider.sh --apply` prints `  FAIL  apply — refused — the aider install ladder is unmeasured in this repo. The documented method is pip install aider-chat into a venv, but no pin, no artefact digest and no measured surface are recorded…` then `AIDER: FAIL (2)`, AIDER_APPLY_EXIT=1; goose prints the same shape (`GOOSE: FAIL (2)`, GOOSE_APPLY_EXIT=1). `find $H -mindepth 1 | wc -l` = 0 and `find $H -type f -perm -u+x | wc -l` = 0 for both.

items.criterion: tests/harness-conformance.sh HARNESSES lists aider and goose so the battery emits a row per harness, and the battery's fail count grows only by those two binary-absent rows (baseline at 6d1d717: 15 pass, 3 fail, 11 skip)
items.detail: tests/harness-conformance.sh:120-121 adds `aider|install-aider.sh|aider|0|(none documented)|0` and `goose|install-goose.sh|goose|0|(none documented)|0`. Base worktree at 6d1d717: `summary: 15 pass, 3 fail, 11 skip` / `HARNESS CONFORMANCE: FAIL (3)`. Head: `summary: 17 pass, 5 fail, 15 skip` / `HARNESS CONFORMANCE: FAIL (5)`, with rows `FAIL aider:check`, `FAIL goose:check`, `PASS aider:vars`, `PASS goose:vars`, `SKIP aider:apply/smoke`, `SKIP goose:apply/smoke`. A row-level diff of the two runs shows only those additions — no third harness changed status.

items.criterion: specs/HARNESS.md (adapter table, closing paragraph, --check table), README.md and docs/handbook/chapters/M5-harness.md state the new truth: both ship a real --check/--contract, --apply refuses by name, still unmeasured
items.detail: `grep -n 'no adapter file' specs/HARNESS.md README.md docs/handbook/chapters/M5-harness.md` returns only specs/HARNESS.md:133 ("aider and goose were the last two with **no adapter file at all**" — past tense, followed by "both now ship install-aider.sh/install-goose.sh") and :181 (the generic rule "A harness the BATTERY names with no adapter file is a FAIL") — neither asserts they currently ship no adapter. Adapter table rows specs/HARNESS.md:118-119 name the two scripts with real --check/--contract and --apply refusal; closing paragraph :131-139; --check table :154-155 gives `FAIL (1)` for both. README.md:137 lists aider, goose as check-only adapters that "print rows and refuse to install anything". docs/handbook/chapters/M5-harness.md:57-64 states both ship a real --check/--contract and refuse --apply by name, with :216 acceptance row and :279-282 inventory entries.

items.criterion: tests/selftest.sh carries a numbered cell that asserts the verdict LETTERS and exit codes for both arms and both harnesses, and bash tests/selftest.sh ends SELFTEST: PASS
items.detail: tests/selftest.sh:5899-5955 adds cell `60. every harness the spec names now has an adapter…`, looping `aider:AIDER goose:GOOSE` and deriving `want`/`wrc` from its own FAIL/WARN counts for both --check and --apply arms (requires exactly one `^LABEL: (PASS|UNVERIFIED|FAIL \(n\))$` line, last line equal to it, exit == wrc, `FAIL apply — refused` row naming 'unmeasured', and 0 executables placed). `bash tests/selftest.sh` tail: `  PASS  aider --check — 1 named row(s), one verdict line 'AIDER: FAIL (1)', exit 1 (the rows require it)` / `  PASS  aider --apply — refused by name (1 row + 'AIDER: FAIL (2)'), exit 1, 0 executable(s) placed in a scratch $HOME` / `  PASS  goose --check — … 'GOOSE: FAIL (1)', exit 1` / `  PASS  goose --apply — … 'GOOSE: FAIL (2)', exit 1, 0 executable(s) placed` / `SELFTEST: PASS`.

items.criterion: both new adapters carry a ch:trace CF-006 marker in their header
items.detail: `grep -c 'ch:trace' scripts/harness/install-aider.sh scripts/harness/install-goose.sh` -> `install-aider.sh:1`, `install-goose.sh:1`; `grep -L 'ch:trace'` on both returns no filenames. The marker is header line 16 of each file: `# ch:trace row=CF-006 spec=specs/HARNESS.md#adapters-and-their-measured-state …`.

items.criterion: --check and --contract place nothing on disk in a scratch HOME (the adapters are read-only outside their own output)
items.detail: With `HOME=$(mktemp -d)`: after `install-aider.sh --check` and `install-goose.sh --check`, `find $H -mindepth 1 | wc -l` = 0; after both `--contract` runs, `files_after=0`. Neither adapter contains a write path (no fetch_verified/curl/mkdir in install-aider.sh or install-goose.sh).

items.criterion: --contract is a real acceptance check, not a stub: it accepts the full §5 set (exit 0) and refuses an incomplete set by name (exit 2), matching install-deepseek.sh
items.detail: With CF_MODEL/CF_PROVIDER/CF_WORKDIR/CF_NAMESPACE/CF_RUN_ID/CF_LANE/CF_API_KEY_FILE set: `aider_contract_full_exit=0` -> `AIDER: CONTRACT PASS — the §5 set is accepted (specs/HARNESS-MATRIX.md §5); nothing installed`, `goose_contract_full_exit=0` -> `GOOSE: CONTRACT PASS`. With the set missing: exit 2 and `  FAIL  contract:required — refused — the §5 run set is incomplete; dropped: CF_MODEL CF_PROVIDER CF_WORKDIR CF_NAMESPACE CF_RUN_ID CF_LANE` — identical to install-deepseek.sh's output for the same input.

items.criterion: the verdict label and exit code are derived from the adapter's own FAIL/WARN row counts via the shared verdict() helper, not hand-written
items.detail: scripts/lib.sh:26-33 verdict() maps FAILED>0 -> `LABEL: FAIL (n)` return 1, WARNED>0 -> `LABEL: UNVERIFIED` return 3, else `LABEL: PASS` return 0; install-aider.sh:110 and install-goose.sh:111 call `verdict AIDER`/`verdict GOOSE` and `exit $?`. Observed counts match: one FAIL row -> `FAIL (1)` exit 1 (--check); two FAIL rows -> `FAIL (2)` exit 1 (--apply). The selftest cell independently re-derives the expected string from the printed rows and passes.

items.criterion: the new adapters are reachable from the provisioning entrypoint (scripts/project-node.sh install-$HARNESS.sh dispatch)
items.detail: scripts/project-node.sh:594-611 builds `inst="$HERE/harness/install-$HARNESS.sh"` and runs it with `--check`/`--apply`. `bash scripts/project-node.sh --project demo --harness aider --check` at head prints `harness: aider (UNVERIFIED adapter)` … `AIDER: FAIL (1)` and `NODE: FAIL (4)`; goose prints `GOOSE: FAIL (1)`. At base 6d1d717 the same command printed `  FAIL  harness:aider — no adapter at scripts/harness/install-aider.sh`, so the new files are now on the live path.

items.criterion: the new selftest cell is registered in the plan and the section-mapping audit stays green
items.detail: `bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh` prints `OK §60 — plan row present`, `arms_plan=63 arms_tree=63`, `RESULT: OK`; docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md:175 carries the §60 row describing the aider/goose adapter cell.
